mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework with Fe(OH) 1D chain SBU built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: At 150 °C without modulator, shorter times (2–48 h) give MOF-235(Fe)/mixed, not MIL-53(Fe). At 120 °C, 72 h gives poor crystallinity; ≥168 h gives MIL-68(Fe) then MIL-53(Fe). Acetic acid prevents MIL-53(Fe); with FeCl2 at 150 °C + AA, dissolution by 48 h and Fe2O3 at 168 h. Fe(NO3)3 at 150 °C, 72 h gives amorphous. Evidence: Fig. 3b; SI Fig. S17, S21–S22; text: “no formation of MIL-53(Fe) when acetic acid is present”.
rationale: Across Fe–terephthalate syntheses (MOF-235(Fe), MIL-53(Fe), [Fe(DMF)(BDC)], [Fe3O(DMF)3(BDC)3][BF4], MIL-88B(Fe), Fe–BDC-Br), failures arise from modulator identity/loading, Fe-source/counterion, and time/temperature. We list explicit amorphous/no-solid and wrong-phase outcomes and boundary-implied non-working settings from the article and SI.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Using NaOH or Et3N bases gave intractable solids; switching to aqueous NH3 afforded crystals.
mof_description: a silver metal-organic framework with Ag4tz6 6-connected SBU + 3-connected Ag and rtl topology built by organic linker 3,5-dipropyl-1,2,4-triazole
modification_notes: For the aqueous?ammonia route to Ag(3,5?Pr2?tz) (method A), replace NH3 with NaOH or Et3N. The paper notes such bases usually give intractable white solids, preventing structure determination. Ammonia volumes are split (4 mL + 2 mL); no explicit base amounts are given here, so amounts are left unspecified.
rationale: Across Ag(3,5-R2-tz) syntheses, using strong bases NaOH or Et3N gave intractable solids; aqueous NH3 enabled crystal growth. We represent these base-identity failures against each successful MOF (Me2, Et2, Pr2, iPr2, Ph2).
time_text: within a couple of days (slow evaporation)

mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with Zn2 paddlewheel SBU; 2-fold interpenetrated built by organic linkers 4-amino-3,5-bis(4-pyridyl)-1,2,4-triazole and 2,5-thiophenedicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Against the MOF-2-Zn solvothermal base, change the stoichiometry to 1:1:1.48 (bpt:H2tdc:Zn) at similar loading (0.546, 0.546, 0.80808 mmol) in 24 mL DMF (Table S9, 2Bulk-4th). PXRD reported “MOF-1-Zn + MOF-2-Zn (minor)”; MOF-2-Zn is the minor phase, i.e., a failure to obtain the target.
rationale: Solvothermal screens at 120 °C, 72 h targeting MOF-2-Zn often yielded MOF-1-Zn or mixed phases. We encode mixture cases where MOF-2-Zn is minor as confirmed failures, plus ambiguous “mixture” cases. One mixture case is also represented against the MOF-1-Zn base.
time_text: 72 h, then cooled to room temperature over 24 h
crystal_morphology: colorless block-shaped crystals (co-produced with MOF-1 plates)

modification_notes: Evidence: Sec. 2.1.2 “1:1:1 resulted in a mixture of MOF-1-Zn and MOF-2-Zn”; SI Table S9 shows many 1:1:1 batches as mixtures, 2Bulk-4th (1:1:1.48, 24 mL) MOF-1+MOF-2 (minor), 5Bulk-2nd (1:1:1.48, 60 mL) mixture, Bulk-1st (1:1:1, 40 mL) mixture; Figures S26–S27. modification_notes: Inferred combination of two separately reported trends for this base: excess Pr(NO3)3 and higher temperature each favor praseodymium formate. Representative cross-product built under the hard ceiling on estimated combinations (3 metal equiv values × 3 temperatures = 9).

modification_notes: Metal precursor screen: only ZrCl4 gave crystalline MIL-161; zirconium(IV) isopropoxide and zirconium(IV) acetylacetonate did not yield crystalline product (article main text). rationale: MIL-161 (Zr6-carboxylate with H2STz) formed in DMF with HCl at 60–80 °C using ZrCl4. Screening showed only ZrCl4 gave crystalline product; other Zr precursors (isopropoxide, acetylacetonate) failed. We capture these precursor failures against the successful MIL-161 recipe.

mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr–oxide chains of 7-coordinated Zr (MIL-140) built by organic linker biphenyl-4,4'-dicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: From field diagrams and PXRD (Figures 6–8; Figure 7; SI Tables S5–S8): without AcOH amorphous/unknown phase; diluted (≥100 eq DMF) with 10–30 eq AcOH gives UiO-67/MIL-140C mixtures; high AcOH at very concentrated (20–40 eq DMF) gives additional phase; modulator screen at 130 eq DMF (0–90 eq AcOH) shows amorphous/UiO-67/mixed phases. article_trial_or_failure_notes: Solvothermal trials failed: UiO-66-(F)4 not obtained; BHC gave clear solutions only.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework built by organic linker 1,2,4,5-benzenetetracarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Authors’ attempts to repeat a previously reported simple water-reflux synthesis of UiO-66-(COOH)2 yielded hard-rock-like products with poor processability and far-from-satisfactory crystallinity. Closest success is the MHT recipe; represent the failed repeat by removing the acetic acid modulator (presence change) while keeping the aqueous reflux (100 °C, 24 h) and other amounts from the base.
rationale: Negative data include: (1) traditional solvothermal attempts failed to form UiO-66-(F)4; (2) BHC gave clear solutions under solvothermal conditions (no solid UiO-66-(COOH)4); (3) repeating a prior water-reflux UiO-66-(COOH)2 method gave hard-rock-like, poorly crystalline products. Plans are anchored to the MHT successes.
washing_cycles: each 3 days at RT, daily solvent exchange

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Solvothermal trials failed: UiO-66-(F)4 not obtained; BHC gave clear solutions only.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework built by organic linker benzene-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexacarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Closest success is MHT UiO-66-(COOH)4. Under traditional solvothermal conditions BHC gave clear solutions only (no solid MOF). modification_notes: After 60 °C incubation, omitting the 105 °C nucleation hold (0 h at 105 °C) led to strong PXRD peak intensity inversion (6.7° vs 9.6° = 100:111) and higher residuals (Figure S9d; Table S4), indicating poor crystallinity. Represented as 105 °C time = 0 h.
rationale: Negative conditions for nano-IRMOF-1 include omitting incubation, direct amine mixing without CTAB, omitting the 105 °C nucleation hold, and substituting TEA with decylamine (2 mmol) which gave no precipitation. solvent_main_amount_text: 50 mL (10 mL aliquot used after incubation)

modification_notes: Evidence basis generalized from the same protocol: text states insufficient thermal treatment (omitting or shortening incubation/nucleation) reduces crystallinity with PXRD peak inversion (Fig. S9; main text). article_trial_or_failure_notes: UiO-type MOF not obtained from Pip-diCO2H despite several trials; DMF-based MOF-74 syntheses gave no crystals before switching conditions.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework with oxo-bridged rod (MOF-74 type) built by organic linker pip-(2,2’-OH)-diCO2H
modification_notes: For Co, DMF-containing solvothermal reactions with pip-(2,2’-OH) yielded no crystalline product. Represent DMF-only and DMF/H2O mixtures; temperatures and times estimated since none were given (solvothermal type; 3 temps × 2 times capped under 12-row rule).
rationale: Negative cases: (1) Pip-diCO2H failed to give a UiO-type Zr MOF despite several trials. (2) For MOF-74 analogs of pip-(2,2’-OH), DMF-containing solvothermal reactions (Mg, Co, Ni, Zn) yielded no crystalline product; successes used water/THF or aqueous NaOH instead.

mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 SBU built by organic linker 1,2,4-benzenetricarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Against the water-reflux base (Success 1), represent the HT closed-vessel condition at 100 °C for 72 h where a large excess of HCl (37%) in H2O prevented MOF formation (Fig. 1a: black = amorphous/recrystallized ligand). We add HCl as a modulator and estimate five high-acid volumes (0.6–1.0 mL of 37% HCl within a 1 mL H2O–HCl mixture) since individual H2O:HCl ratios were not listed.
rationale: High-throughput (HT) screening at 100 °C, 72 h showed that a large excess of HCl (37%) in H2O prevents formation of UiO-66(Zr)–(COOH)x, yielding amorphous or recrystallized ligand. Plans convert these non-working, high-acidity conditions against the water-reflux bases for UiO-66(Zr)-(COOH) and UiO-66(Zr)-(COOH)2.
vessel_type: 50 mL round-bottom flask with reflux condenser
washing_cycles: dispersed in water (10 mL per 1 g) and refluxed 16 h; then washed with water

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Low 2-MIM (0.199 M) gave Co(OH)2 nanosheets (no ZIF-67).
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework built by organic linker 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Against the 80 °C CTAB/TMB emulsion recipe for ZIF-67 meso-/microNBs, lowering 2-MIM concentration to 0.199 M (0.5 mL used; 0.0995 mmol) produced hexagonal Co(OH)2 nanosheets with no ZIF-67 (Fig. S16a,d; main text). Linker amount computed from 0.5 mL × 0.199 M.
rationale: Paper reports ZIF-67 nanobowls assembled at TMB/H2O interfaces using CTAB. The only clear synthesis failure is very low 2-methylimidazole (2-MIM), which gives Co(OH)2 nanosheets (no ZIF-67). We map this against the 80 °C meso-/microNBs base.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Low 2-MIM (0.199 M) gave Co(OH)2 nanosheets (no ZIF-67).
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework built by organic linker 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Evidence: SI text and Fig. S16a,d general rule—0.199 M 2-MIM insufficient; Co(OH)2 nanosheets form under the aqueous CTAB/TMB protocol, implying failure of ZIF formation at low linker.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Without FA or with no surfactant, obtained amorphous/unknown mesoporous phase; no crystalline MOF or mesostructure.

modification_notes: Remove formic acid (FA/Zr = 0) while keeping CAPB, water, 60 °C, 24 h. Reported outcome: only an unidentified mesoporous phase; no wide-angle crystalline peaks (main text; Figure S7a).

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Direct syntheses with other first-row metals (Co2+, Ni2+, Cu2+) to form isomorphous frameworks were unsuccessful; used post-synthetic metal exchange instead.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework with Zn–porphyrin chains bridged by nitrate; layers linked by BDC (2D) built by organic linkers 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(4-pyridyl)porphyrin and terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Metal-ion metathesis section states isomorphous analogues of 1 with other first-row transition elements, using similar solvothermal protocols, were not obtained. rationale: Direct solvothermal attempts to prepare isomorphous analogues of Zn–TPyP MOFs 1–3 with other first?row transition metals failed; we represent these as metal-identity substitutions against each successful Zn base recipe.
metal_cluster_connectivity: Zn–porphyrin chains bridged by nitrate; layers linked by BDC (2D)

modification_notes: Evidence extrapolated under authors’ stated rules: water is required to avoid phase separation; methanol drove microporous ZIF-8 (text 2.2.4, Fig. S56). article_trial_or_failure_notes: Isostructural Ce-CP using H2cba could not be obtained despite varying pH, metal/solvent ratio, temperature, time, and base amount.
mof_description: a cerium metal-organic framework with CeO9 nodes; 2D layers, (4,4,4,6,6)-connected net built by organic linker 4,4?-methylenebenzoic acid
modification_notes: Linker swap: H2obb ? 4,4?-methylenebenzoic acid (H2cba). Article states isostructural Ce-CP could not be obtained under same or changed conditions (pH, metal/solvent ratio, temperature, time, base amount) (main text; SI Fig. S7). We enumerate representative solvothermal temperatures (120, 160 °C) and times (24, 48 h) with three metal:linker ratios computed by holding linker at 0.35 mmol: 0.25:1 (Ce = 0.0875 mmol), base-like ~0.53:1 (Ce = 0.185 mmol), and 1:1 (Ce = 0.35 mmol). Other varied factors (pH, solvent ratio, base amount) were reported but not further enumerated here to respect the hard ?12-row ceiling on estimated combinations.
rationale: Paper reports Ce-CP from H2obb; isostructural Ce-CP with H2cba could not be obtained despite varying pH, metal/solvent ratio, temperature, time, and base amount. We model this as a linker swap (H2cba) with representative solvothermal temperature/time and metal:linker ratios anchored to the successful base recipe.
vessel_type: Teflon-lined autoclave (Parr, 20 mL), sealed in stainless-steel vessel
stirring: stirred 15 min at RT, then static during heating
activation_text: EtOH exchange at 80 °C for 12 h; activated under vacuum at 240 °C for 12 h (for LAB-Ce-CP)

modification_notes: Base: complex 6-like conditions. Evidence: text: “no suitable crystals… only CuII complexes were constructed.” pH window for 2, 3 and 6: text: “the pH from 3.5 to 4.0 … suitable crystals … can be obtained.” Variations include NiII/CdII/MnII swaps and pH outside 3.5–4.0 (fail).

activation_text: dried in a desiccator at room temperature
metal_cluster_connectivity: TeMo6 hexadentate nodes linked by Cu; 3,4,6-connected net

rationale: Negative conditions target hierarchical ZIF-8 (H-ZIF-8) made in water with TEA/CTAB/His. The paper states CTAB or His alone failed to form hierarchical pores, and substituting His with arginine (with CTAB) gave no mesopores. These are represented against the successful H-ZIF-8 recipe.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: CTAB or His alone did not produce hierarchical porosity in ZIF-8.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with sod topology built by organic linker 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Evidence: text: “No typically hierarchical porous structure was formed in the presence of either the CTAB or His separately.” A-ZIF-8 (Arg instead of His) showed no hysteresis loops (Fig. S1). Also, authors stress CTAB–His dual templating is necessary for mesoporosity.
rationale: For hierarchical ZIF-8 (H-ZIF-8) in water, both CTAB and L-histidine are required. CTAB alone, His alone, or substituting His with arginine (A-ZIF-8) did not yield mesoporosity. We list these negative conditions against the successful ZIF-8 and H-ZIF-8 protocols from 10.1039/c3nr04390h.

mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 SBU built by organic linker 4,4?-azobenzenedicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: No monocarboxylate modulator added (only water present as in base). rationale: UiO-AZB required a monocarboxylate modulator (AA/FA/BA) to crystallize under solvothermal DMF conditions; attempts without any modulator gave amorphous PXRD. Plans capture the modulator-omitted condition relative to a working acetic-acid recipe.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: NH3 base gave amorphous Co3(HITP)2; no precipitate without air; crystallinity optimized by CH3CO2Na and mixed solvents.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework built by organic linker 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene hexahydrochloride
modification_notes: Adding 3 eq of stronger bases (pyridine, 2,2?-bipyridine, o-phenylenediamine, ethylenediamine) as additional modulators alongside NaOAc led to less crystalline or amorphous Co3(HITP)2 (Figure S2d). Represented by adding each as modulator_2 (3 eq = 0.0279 mmol).
rationale: Negative conditions include no-air (no precipitate), ammonia base yielding amorphous/low-crystallinity products, substituting NaOAc with NaOTf, adding strong amine modulators, and nonoptimal solvent systems (water-only or wrong coordinating solvent) giving poorer crystallinity, for Co3(HITP)2, Ni3(HITP)2, and Cu3(HITP)2.
metal_1_amount_text: stock solution 62.1 mmol·L?1 in DMF, 1.5 mL (10 eq.)
modulator_1_amount_text: 2 mL of 2 mol·L?1 aqueous solution (added after HATP)

mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework built by organic linker 3-carboxy-1-(3,5-dicarboxybenzyl)pyridinium bromide
modification_notes: Compound 3 bulk attempt gave a heterogeneous mixture: “phase pure bulk material was not successful … different phases … could not be separated.” Represented as substituting Cu(CH3COO)2·2H2O for Cd(CH3COO)2 in the L1 bulk recipe (SUCCESS 1: H2O 5 mL, conc. rationale: Bulk, phase-pure synthesis failed for compounds 3 (Cu–L1), 5 (Co–L2), and 7 (Cd–L2), yielding heterogeneous mixtures. We represent these as metal-identity substitutions into the paper’s working hydrothermal bulk protocols for L1 and L2.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: HT screen for UiO-68 single crystals: only 40 equiv TFA at 100 °C for 72 h gave crystals; other conditions failed or gave poor crystallinity.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 12-connected SBU and fcu topology built by organic linkers [1,1?:4?,1?-terphenyl]-4,4?-dicarboxylic acid and 4,4?-(1,2,4,5-tetrazine-3,6-diyl)dibenzoic acid
modification_notes: Direct de novo mixed-linker synthesis: add H2TZDC as a second linker (keeping TPDC) and use DMF alone or DMF/NMP, 100 °C, 48 h, TFA 24–40 equiv. SI S5.1 reports reduced crystallinity, negligible TZDC incorporation, and unreacted linker bands (no crystalline mixed-linker product).
rationale: HT screening for UiO-68 single crystals found only one working point (TFA 40 equiv, 100 °C, 72 h). We capture nearby non-working conditions: other acids, shorter time, higher temperature, no modulator, and direct mixed-linker de novo attempts, all reported to give no/poor crystallinity.
activation_text: Hexane exchange 3 days; dried at room temperature

modification_notes: Shorten time to 48 h at 100 °C with TFA. Table S1 lists TFA 0–80, 20, 40 equiv at 48 h; all failed to give UiO-68 crystals. Only 72 h at 40 equiv worked.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Attempts to synthesize MOF 3 directly were unsuccessful.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework built by organic linker 3-(2?-pyridyl)-5-(4??-pyridyl)-1,2,4-triazole
modification_notes: Direct solvothermal synthesis attempts for polymorph 3 were unsuccessful. Represented as changing the mixed solvent to DMF/H2O = 1:9 (0.6/5.4 mL) at 130 °C, 24 h, keeping metal/linker amounts as in base 1. Volumes chosen to match the article’s 1:9 ratio used for transforming 1?3; specific direct-synthesis volumes not stated.
rationale: DMF/H2O ratio controls Co–Hdpt24 products. Compounds 1 (9:1) and 2 (1:1) are accessible directly, but all direct attempts to obtain polymorph 3 failed. We model a direct-synthesis try at 1:9 DMF/H2O against base 1.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Attempts to synthesize MOF 3 directly were unsuccessful.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework built by organic linker 3-(2′-pyridyl)-5-(4′′-pyridyl)-1,2,4-triazole
modification_notes: Base: direct synthesis of 1 at DMF/H2O 9:1. Evidence: text: “all of our attempts to synthesize 3 directly were unsuccessful”; text: “at 4:1 and 3:2, mixed crystals of 1 and 2; at 2:3, mixed crystals of 2 and 3.” Using same stoichiometry and total volume, vary DMF to set failing ratios.
rationale: For Co–Hdpt24 complexes 1–4, DMF/H2O ratio dictates products. Outside 9:1 (1), 1:1 (2), and 0:1 (4), mixtures or non-target phases occur; direct synthesis of 3 (1:9) was unsuccessful. We compile non-working solvent ratios relative to each successful base.

mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework with Ni2 paddlewheel hexagonal sheets built by organic linker isophthalic acid
modification_notes: Article states: “The reaction of nickel(II) or cobalt(II) salts with H2 tBu-bdc … afforded … a strictly amorphous material for the latter (Co2+).” Represented by substituting representative cobalt(II) salts for the base’s nickel(II) acetate in Ni(tBu-bdc). article_trial_or_failure_notes: H2dhbq starting material gave only amorphous solid
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework with two interpenetrated (10,3)-a nets built by organic linker 2,5-diaminobenzoquinone
modification_notes: Neutral pH (no HCl acidification): remove the HCl modulator used to adjust pH to 3 in the base. Under pH-neutral conditions, an unidentified ferromagnetic impurity co-precipitated with 1, preventing clean analysis; treated as a failure (not phase-pure target).
rationale: For (NBu4)2FeIII2(dhbq)3, failures include: using H2dhbq as the starting linker gave amorphous solids; neutral pH (no HCl) led to co-precipitation of an unidentified ferromagnetic impurity with 1; smaller quaternary ammonium countercations (tetrapropylammonium, methyltributylammonium) failed to form the 3D framework.

modification_notes: Relative to the successful synthesis of 2, decrease pyridine to 1–2 equiv. The article states at least 3 equiv were required to obtain 2 (Fig. S7); thus 1–2 equiv did not yield 2. Pyridine amounts computed from the base Cu amount (0.4 mmol): 1 eq = 0.4 mmol; 2 eq = 0.8 mmol.
rationale: Negative data focus on pyridine stoichiometry for forming compound 2: too little pyridine (<3 equiv) failed to give 2; too much gave the copper–pyridine nitrate complex instead. Both are represented as modifications of the successful solvothermal recipe for 2.

modification_notes: Main text: “under identical reaction conditions, single metals such as Mg, V, Mn, and Co fail to form crystalline MOFs.” Negative variants keep BPDC/DMF/AA and 140 °C, 3 d while swapping to single-metal feeds (Co, Mn, V, Mg).
rationale: MIL-126 heterometallic syntheses succeeded, but the paper states monometallic Mg, V, Mn, and Co do not crystallize under identical DMF/AA solvothermal conditions. We enumerate these explicitly failed single-metal swaps against each successful MIL-126(Fe/x) or (V/x) protocol.

mof_description: a titanium metal-organic framework with cyclic Ti8O8 oxo cluster built by organic linker 2,5-diaminoterephthalic acid
modification_notes: Attempt with only the diaminated linker: from the successful mixed mono+di aminated base, remove the monoaminated linker so that only 2,5-diaminoterephthalic acid is present. Reported outcome was amorphous. Linker shift follows the schema rule for omitting the first linker.
rationale: Failures concern attempts to incorporate 2,5-diaminoterephthalic acid (BDC-(NH2)2) into MIL-125: BDC + diamino mixtures gave very poor crystallinity across varied T/time/ratios, and diamino-only gave amorphous solids. Mixed mono+di linkers succeeded; BDC or BDC+monoamino bases anchor the negative plans.
washing_cycles: 2×10 mL DMF, then 10 mL MeOH; dried at 70 °C
activation_text: Heated in 20 mL DMF at 150 °C for 24 h, then washed with 10 mL DMF and 10 mL MeOH and dried at 70 °C

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Agitation without HF did not yield Fe(BDC)(DMF,F); 5–6 days under agitation gave hematite.
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Prolong the base Fe(BDC)(DMF,F) stirred synthesis (150 °C, DMF, HF) to 5–6 days. ESI Fig. S1 reports only hematite (?-Fe2O3) under these times; no linker-containing MOF formed. Represented as a time list against the base.
rationale: Paper studies MIL-53(Fe), Fe(BDC)(DMF,F), and NH2-MIL-53(Fe). Failures include hematite formation upon prolonged agitation in the Fe(BDC)(DMF,F) route, and markedly lower crystallinity for NH2-MIL-53(Fe) without HF.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Agitation without HF did not yield Fe(BDC)(DMF,F); 5–6 days under agitation gave hematite.
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Direct failures: without HF under agitation Fe(BDC)(DMF,F) does not form (Fig. 2, sample d; text: “could not be prepared successfully without HF”). Time screen under agitation: 1 d gives MIL-53(Fe), 2 d mixed, 4 d degraded crystallinity, 5–6 d hematite only (Fig. 3; SI Fig. S1).
rationale: Failures cluster around Fe(BDC)(DMF,F): HF is essential under agitation and time outside 3 days gives wrong phases or hematite. MIL-53(Fe) and NH2-MIL-53(Fe) show only crystallinity changes without HF, not outright failures under reported conditions.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: UiO-66 crystals could not be obtained when HF > 3 eq was added
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 12-connected SBU built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Failure boundary stated: >3 eq HF gives no UiO-66. Using the fluorine-free base (Success 10, 0 eq HF), add hydrofluoric acid (40%) at representative values beyond the 3 eq threshold (4, 5, 6, 8, 10 eq). Volumes estimated from Table S1 for this composition where 1 eq = 0.039 mL; amounts listed are 0.039 mL × eq.
rationale: UiO-66 solvothermal synthesis in DMF: authors report that adding >3 eq HF relative to ZrCl4 prevents obtaining UiO-66. Represented by adding HF at 4–10 eq to the fluorine-free base recipe.

mof_description: a calcium metal-organic framework with 8-coordinate Ca(II) nodes; Ca–O and Ca–N links; 1D channels built by organic linker 5-(1,2,4-triazoleyl)isophthalic acid
modification_notes: Pure DMF (no water) was used with Ca(OAc)2 and 5TIA; the solution was kept at 30, 60, 90, and 120 °C for 2 days in each case, yielding white gels (article synthesis of Ca-5TIA-Gel). Represented against the Ca-5TIA-MOF base by removing water.
rationale: Ca-5TIA-MOF crystallizes in mixed DMF/H2O. Pure DMF or very low H2O contents gave gels or precipitates, not the crystalline MOF. We capture these non-working solvent compositions and temperatures against the Ca-5TIA-MOF base recipe.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Excess H2O or acetic acid gave no product within 15 min (Table S1); short times for PCN-222 gave disordered solids.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 cluster built by organic linker 2-aminoterephthalic acid
modification_notes: Fast UiO-66-NH2 at 120 °C for 15 min without added H2O (0 ?L) gave no precipitate/product within 15 min (Fig. 2a; Table S1). Represents removal of the water modulator.
rationale: Missing H2O in fast UiO-66-NH2 or BUT-12 gave no product in 15 min; reference PCN-222-Ni at 6 h gave only disordered solids. Excess H2O/AcOH or high H2O led to disordered/no product but vary only modulator amounts, hence excluded.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: No solid formed under similar solvothermal conditions without formate even after 3 months.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework built by organic linker 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Direct failure from text: “solvothermal reactions in the absence of formate under otherwise similar conditions did not yield solid material even after prolonged periods of time (3 months).” All syntheses with formate (0.5–4.0 eq) and 120–140 °C gave pure ZIF-8 (Fig. S1).
rationale: For solvothermal ZIF-8 (ZnCl2/Hmim/NaHCO2 in MeOH), the article states that omitting formate yields no solid even after 3 months, while 0.5–4.0 eq formate at 120–140 °C gives pure ZIF-8. Negative plan targets modulator omission under the successful protocol.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: No solid formed under similar solvothermal conditions without formate even after 3 months.

modification_notes: Omit sodium formate (modulator) from the solvothermal MeOH synthesis; article states no solid formed even after 3 months under otherwise similar conditions. Built by removing modulator_1 and setting time to the reported 3 months; other parameters anchored to SUCCESS 1.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: No solid formed under similar solvothermal conditions without formate even after 3 months.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework built by organic linker 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Main text: “solvothermal reactions in the absence of formate … did not yield solid material even after … 3 months.” Also: all monitored syntheses with NaHCO2 (x=0.5–4.0) and 120–140 °C gave pure ZIF-8 (Fig. S1).
rationale: For solvothermal ZIF-8 in MeOH, authors report a clear negative: without formate modulator, no solid forms even after 3 months. All tested temperatures (120–140 °C) and NaHCO2 loadings (x=0.5–4.0) produced ZIF-8, so the key failure is absence of formate.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Prehydrolyzed (SO3H)(SO2)obaH2 precursor gave a nonisostructural Cd material, not JUK-13-SO3H-SO2.
mof_description: a cadmium metal-organic framework with dicadmium nodes; 7-coordinate Cd built by organic linkers terephthalaldehyde di-isonicotinoylhydrazone and (SO3H)(SO2)obaH2
modification_notes: Substitute the prehydrolyzed dicarboxylate (SO3H)(SO2)obaH2 for the chlorosulfonyl precursor used in the successful recipe, under otherwise similar DMF/H2O solvothermal conditions (9:1 v/v). Using the SI-stated scaled amounts and shorter time (80 °C, 2 days) yielded a nonisostructural crystalline Cd material (insufficient for SCXRD), not JUK-13-SO3H-SO2; IR shows coordinated sulfonate and CO2/H2O uptakes are strongly reduced (main text; SI Figures S7–S9).
rationale: Capture the failed solvothermal attempt to make JUK-13-SO3H-SO2 using the prehydrolyzed (SO3H)(SO2)obaH2 linker instead of the chlorosulfonyl precursor; it gave a nonisostructural Cd material, not the target MOF.

modification_notes: Crystals could not be obtained when final pH <6 or >7. Here represented by changing the basic modulator: replace KOH with HCl (acidification, pH<6) or with a stronger base TMAH (pH>7). Py retained. Amounts carried from the KOH slot; other conditions unchanged.
rationale: Negative conditions for Cd/H3IDC/bpy hydrothermal MOFs: off-stoichiometric feeds generally failed or gave ~2% yield, and crystals were unobtainable when final pH <6 or >7. article_trial_or_failure_notes: Direct mixing of K2[M(SCN)4] with Fe(II)-pz (MeOH/H2O) gave highly insoluble microcrystalline powders; single crystals required slow diffusion.
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework with flat {Fe[Pd(SCN)4]} layers pillared by pyrazine (3D) built by organic linker pyrazine
modification_notes: Against the base recipe for 2, use the MeOH/H2O solvent pair reported for the direct-mixing trials: adding aqueous K2[M(SCN)4] (M = Pd or Pt) into methanolic Fe–pz (1:1) gave highly insoluble microcrystalline powders with no identified crystalline product. Mixing vs. slow diffusion cannot be encoded; solvents are captured. Pt salt included per text; its amount taken equal to Pd in the base.
rationale: Targets {Fe(MeOH)2[Pd(SCN)4]}·pz (1a) and {Fe(pz)[Pd(SCN)4]} (2) via slow diffusion. Direct addition of aqueous K2[M(SCN)4] to methanolic Fe–pz (1:1) gave insoluble microcrystalline powders; MeOH diffusion yielded 1a (alternate to 2). We capture the direct-mixing outcome against base 2; alternate-phase cases are excluded.

mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 12-connected SBU built by organic linker pbdc-9a
modification_notes: Substitute saturated longer-spacer polymer ligands pbdc-9a or pbdc-10a for pbdc-8a in the same DEF/formic acid solvothermal recipe. The article reports only amorphous materials for both linkers (bundled same-outcome substitutions). Linker amounts retained from base.
rationale: Failures arise when the polymer linker spacing is too long. pbdc-10a-u gave amorphous films under several conditions; saturated pbdc-9a and pbdc-10a gave only amorphous products. Plans substitute these linkers into the standard DEF/formic acid ZrCl4 solvothermal recipe for polyUiO-66.
washing_cycles: DMF exchange 3× over 1 day; MeOH exchange 2×/day for 2 days

modification_notes: Figure 2b states a threshold surfactant amount is required; below it, zinc alkaline nitrate forms at 60 °C with Zn/H-MeIM = 1:2. To represent the sub-threshold case without modulator-amount-only variation, the surfactant mixture is omitted entirely (zero is below threshold).

rationale: Negative conditions for CAU-1-(OH)2 include low-concentration trials (high MeOH filling levels with small reagent charges) and NaOH-additive amounts other than 50 ?L, which failed to give crystalline CAU-1-(OH)2 at 125 °C, 5 h. modification_notes: Starting from the ZnSO4 system at Zn2+:MIm:NH3 = 1:2:50, adding Na2SO4 at 5 or 10 equiv still gave mixed ZIF-8/dia(Zn); pure ZIF-8 formed only at Zn2+:Na2SO4 = 1:15 (Fig. 4a).
rationale: ZIF-8 in aqueous NH3: failures captured include insufficient added anions (Na2SO4, NaOAc, NaCl) at specified NH3 giving ZIF-8/dia(Zn) mixtures, and NaNO3 addition failing to yield pure ZIF-8. Low-NH3-only failures are noted but excluded as modulator-amount-only.
activation_text: Evacuated at 250 °C under vacuum for 4 h

article_trial_or_failure_notes: 473 conditions screened in 96-well plates; many did not form wet gels or target phases.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework built by organic linkers benzimidazole and 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Failures supported by HTE/modeling: CoAc reduces gelation (Table 2: M1_CoAc negative); water as metal solvent suppresses gelation (Table 2: M1_sol_water negative); substituting mim with bim often yields dry solids in im–bim screens (Table S1; Figs. S2–S5).
rationale: Negative conditions are drawn from the paper’s 96‑well HTE and modeling for ZIF-zni and ZIF-61 gels: water as metal solvent and Co2+ suppress gelation; several linkers (dcim, pr, bim) gave dry solids; some im–bim substitutions failed. Evidence: Tables S1–S7, Fig. 6, Table 2, Figs. S2–S15.
activation_text: Supernatant removed; wet precipitate dried overnight at RT to obtain gel; gel solidified/crystallized by heating to 150 °C

mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework with infinite Cu–O double chains (ladder-like), ?3-O bridges and kgd topology built by organic linker isonicotinic acid
modification_notes: Directly replacing the in situ-cleaving linker with INA as the feedstock under the same solvothermal conditions gave no target crystals. Represented by substituting linker identity to isonicotinic acid (INA) at the base 0.1 mmol; other reagents/conditions unchanged.

mof_description: a cerium metal-organic framework with 9-coordinate Ce; helical chains cross-linked built by organic linker pyridine-2,4,6-tricarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Hydrothermal base recipe (Success 1: Ce(SO4)2·4H2O + H3PTC in H2O, 180 °C) with triethylamine replaced by sodium hydroxide. Article reports only Na3PTC crystals (no Ce–PTC MOF) by SCXRD (CCDC 2110896). NaOH amount not stated; other conditions assumed as base.
rationale: Hydrothermal Ce–PTC MOFs (compounds (1) and (2)) succeed with triethylamine base; using NaOH base gave only Na3PTC (no Ce–PTC framework). We capture this failed hydrothermal condition against the closest successful recipe.

modification_notes: Substitute the successful linker (H23) with shorter H21 or H22 under the same copper–DMF solvothermal recipe the paper explicitly uses for H21–H25 (DMF, 110 °C, 36 h; 10% linker excess). modification_notes: Evidence: text: "use of N,N-dimethylformamide as a solvent led to different crystalline phases whose crystal structures could not be solved yet"; text: "catechol... shall not be used as a modulator" (it inserts, forming MIL-168); text: "An increase of the pH did not lead, however, to any crystalline materials"; SI Fig. S1 shows poor crystallinity under AcOH/DEA conditions.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: At 130 °C with 24–32% H2O no crystals formed; at 150 °C with ≥24% H2O a Sr-bc coordination polymer formed instead of the target MOF.
mof_description: a strontium metal-organic framework with infinite Sr-carboxylate chains (1D SBU) built by organic linker 2,2′-dinitro-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4,4′-dicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Evidence: Table 1 entries 2–3: 24% or 32% H2O at 130 °C for 72 h gave no crystal formation. Table 1 entries 4–6: ≥24% H2O at 150 °C for 96 h yielded Sr-bc/bcNO coordination polymer, not WUF-16. Text: “for WUF-16 a water content of 24% or above resulted in no crystal growth”.

modification_notes: Vary metal source away from Mn(II) acetate: text: starting from Mn12(Acetate) gives PCN-47; using KMnO4 gives PCN-49 (wrong phases for PCN-48). No explicit failed solvent/modulator/time windows reported.
rationale: For PCN-47/48/49 with TCPS in DMF and acetic acid, swapping Mn source yields different phases, not the target. washing_cycles: DMF 3× by centrifugation; MeOH 3×/day for 3 d; CH2Cl2 3×/day for 3 d
activation_text: under vacuum at room temperature for 24 h

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Fe2(dobpdc) and Cu2(dobpdc) not obtained from FeO or CuO under these conditions.
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework built by organic linker 4,4?-dihydroxy-(1,1?-biphenyl)-3,3?-dicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Metal-identity substitutions in the authors' oxide-to-MOF powder route (DMF 0.20 mL, H4(dobpdc) 0.10 mmol, 120 °C): CoO (base) replaced by FeO or CuO. The paper states attempts to yield Fe2(dobpdc) and Cu2(dobpdc) under these conditions were not immediately successful.
rationale: Minute-MOF oxide-to-M2(dobpdc) syntheses succeeded for Mg, Zn, Co, Mn, Ni in DMF at 120 °C. Attempts using FeO or CuO powders to make Fe2(dobpdc) or Cu2(dobpdc) under the same conditions were unsuccessful; we represent these as metal-identity substitutions vs the powder-based base.
activation_text: 250 °C under dynamic vacuum (<20 µTorr) for 12 h

modification_notes: General statement that attempts with other lanthanide ions beyond Sm/Eu/Gd/Tb/Dy/Ho/Er did not yield isomorphous complexes. mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework built by organic linker 1,4-bis(1H-pyrazol-4-yl)-2-hydroxybenzene
modification_notes: Microwave i-PrOH precursor screen (Section 3.1, Fig. S3): ZnCl2 and Zn(NO3)2·6H2O produced amorphous products by PXRD. Represented as substitutions of the zinc source under the same microwave conditions and amounts as Success 5.

mof_description: a cerium metal-organic framework with CeO9 nodes; [Ce2(tar)2] dimers; sulfate-pillared built by organic linker DL-tartaric acid
modification_notes: Evidence: text: 'employing CeO2 yielded Ce2(SO4)3·5H2O, using Ce2(SO4)3 obtained polymer 5' and 'employing CeO2 resulted in the α-phase while choosing Ce2(SO4)3 got the β-phase' (Syntheses). Swapping to DL-tartrate or to Ce2(SO4)3 leads to non-1 products.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Only polymorph 3 was isolated pure; polymorph 2 obtained once and could not be reproduced; most syntheses gave mixtures of polymorphs and a Cu(II) phase.
mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework with Cu2Cl2 dinuclear node (CuI) and hcb topology built by organic linker bis(4-pyridylthio)methane
modification_notes: Kinetic polymorph 2 converts toward 1 upon extended heating: a 1+2 mixture became 1-major after a further 10 h at 115 °C. Represented as increasing time from 10 h to 20 h at 115 °C in water (no additives).
rationale: Negative plans capture polymorph-selectivity failures in the CuCl(4bpytm) system: low-T/time mixtures of 1+3, additive-induced shift to 1, and decomposition at 150 °C/30 h. Also, metastable 2 converts toward 1 upon extended heating.

mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 6-connected layers; (3,6)-connected network built by organic linker 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene
modification_notes: Within the reported modulator-identity × water-addition screen (Table S1, entries for AA/PA/CA with 0, 0.25, 0.5 mL H2O; 10 mg ZrCl4, 10 mg BTB, DMF 3 mL, 120 °C 48 h), samples using acetic, propanoic, or caproic acid produced low-crystallinity Zr-BTB with irregular particles and low surface areas (text; Fig. 2b,c; Figs. modification_notes: Direct synthesis with an unprotected proline-substituted bpdc linker (no Boc) in place of H2L was reported as not successful. Represented by substituting H2L-NHPro for H2L at the base amount under identical solvothermal conditions (DEF, 100 °C, 48 h).
rationale: Unprotected proline-functionalized linker failed to form the DUT-32 derivative; Boc protection enabled successful DUT-32-NHProBoc formation. We map the failed direct synthesis (unprotected proline linker) against the DUT-32-NHProBoc base in DEF at 100 °C for 48 h.
activation_text: Solvent exchange to acetone or amyl acetate, CO2 exchange, followed by supercritical drying

modification_notes: Against the successful MOF-808-FA recipe (H2O 10 mL, FA 10 mL, conc. HCl 100 ?L; 110 °C, 18 h), removing the conc. HCl additive (H2O/FA 1:1, no HCl) produced gel-like impurities and a lower BET area (1510 m2/g). Source: main text and Figure S4.
rationale: Hydrothermal MOF-808 synthesis: omission of concentrated HCl in H2O/formic acid (1:1) gave gel-like impurities and low porosity. We represent this against the corresponding successful HCl-added MOF-808-FA recipe.
washing_cycles: water replaced six times over 24 h; ethanol 3×

mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework built by organic linker 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Against the ZIF-8 monolith base with n-butylamine (20 mmol), substitute a mixed-modulator system: add 1-methylimidazole (10 mmol) and reduce n-butylamine to 10 mmol, keeping MeOH, RT, and 24 h. rationale: Paper studies ZIF-8/67 powders and monoliths. Mixed-modulator ZIF-8 (n-butylamine + 1-methylimidazole) produced an almost entirely amorphous, functionally non-porous material; we represent this as a failure relative to the successful n-butylamine-only monolith base.
activation_text: air dried under ambient temperature and pressure for 72 h (monolith formation)

mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework with [Zn3(COO)6] trinuclear SBU built by organic linkers tris(4?-carboxybiphenyl)amine and 3,5-di(pyridin-4-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-4-amine
modification_notes: Against success 1 (1:1:4 H3L:dpta:Zn in DMF, 90 °C, 72 h), Zn(NO3)2·6H2O was substituted with Cu(NO3)2·3H2O. The article states direct de novo synthesis of 1Cu was unsuccessful; only SC–SC Cu2+ exchange yielded 1Cu. Cu salt mmol set equal to base Zn mmol per AMOUNTS rule.
rationale: Direct de novo solvothermal syntheses of Cu(II) analogues (1Cu, 2Cu) by substituting Cu(NO3)2·3H2O for Zn(NO3)2·6H2O under the DMF/90 °C/72 h protocols used for 1 and 2 were unsuccessful; only SC–SC Cu2+ transmetalation produced 1Cu and 2Cu.
activation_text: Acetone exchange 5 days at RT, then 120 °C under vacuum for 12 h

article_trial_or_failure_notes: ZIF-20 crystallized only at pH 10–11; no mineral formed outside this range.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with sod topology built by organic linker 2-methylimidazole
modification_notes: Lowered concentrations to the biomineralization screen (neutral water, 160 mM HmIm and 40 mM ZnAc2·2H2O; 2 mL each). Authors report no precipitate without protein (main text Fig. 1c). Amounts computed from stated molarity × 2 mL; RT and 4 h carried from base.
rationale: At the biomineralization screening ratio (linker 160 mM : Zn 40 mM) in neutral water and room temperature, ZIF-8, ZIF-90, and ZIF-zni did not precipitate without protein. modification_notes: Organic-base pH adjustments under pure H2O, DMF, or MeOH gave powders or H4BDP crystals. Represented vs success 2 using four representative organic bases (class substitution); temperature fixed at base value (150 °C); secondary solvent removed.

rationale: Captures the single reported non-working condition: Mn2+/H4BTC solvothermal reaction without TTP (otherwise identical DMF/H2O, HCl, 100 °C, 72 h) yielded an unidentified powder (compound 3). Post-synthesis thermal collapse of 1/2/4 after heating is listed but excluded.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: HT screening: pure H2O gave linker recrystallization; several conditions produced unknown byproducts; sulfate source occluded in pores for polar linkers.
mof_description: an aluminum metal-organic framework with cis-connected corner-sharing AlO6 helical chains (Al–OH chains) built by organic linker isophthalic acid
modification_notes: HT discovery for CAU-10-H with AlCl3·6H2O at 145 °C, 12 h in 4:1 H2O/DMF (500 µL total) gave impure product or recrystallized linker across ratios (SI VI, Fig. S35). washing_cycles: redispersed by sonication and stirring; filtered again

article_trial_or_failure_notes: D2c showed trapped free linker; D2e (70% L2 feed) contained impurities.
mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework built by organic linkers benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid and 5-cyanoisophthalic acid
modification_notes: Built on D2 base (Cu(NO3)2, DMF/EtOH 1:1 + H2O, 70 °C, 12 h). Sample D2c prepared with 50% L2 feed contained trapped free L2 (SI Table S1; SI Fig. S2, S3b). Using the reported total linker charge (H3BTC + L2 = 1.076 mmol), the 50% feed corresponds to H3BTC 0.538 mmol and L2 0.538 mmol (amounts computed from the stated feed ratio).
rationale: Negative conditions for DEMOF D2 (HKUST-1 doped with 5-cyanoisophthalate): a 50% L2 feed gave trapped free linker; a 70% L2 feed led to impurities. Both mapped to the D2 successful solvothermal base (Cu(NO3)2, DMF/EtOH/H2O, 70 °C, 12 h).

mof_description: a cadmium metal-organic framework with gis topology built by organic linker 3-(pyridin-3-yloxy)benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Against the water/KOH (0.3 mmol), 170 °C, 72 h synthesis of 1, the paper states that changing pH and temperature gave low yields or unidentified precipitates. pH shifts represented by substituting the base with representative stronger/weaker acid/base modulators (HCl, acetic acid, ammonia solution, triethylamine) at the same molar amount; temperatures represented by 3 plausible hydrothermal values (140, 150, 190 °C). Combined to reflect the joint pH+T variation described.
rationale: Failures reported when altering pH and temperature from the water/KOH hydrothermal syntheses of Cd–pbda frameworks [Cd(pbda)]n (1) and [Cd3(OH)2(pbda)2]n (2): low yields or unidentified precipitates. Represented via modulator-identity swaps (acid/weaker base) and temperature changes.

rationale: Negative data captured: replacing the enantiopure linker H2L with its other diastereomer under DUT-129 solvothermal conditions gave an X-ray amorphous product. modification_notes: Addition of NH3·H2O accelerated kinetics and produced numerous irregular ZIF-90 nanoparticles (main text; SI Fig. S8,S12). Built as adding ammonium hydroxide alongside PEO-b-PS at the high-H2O condition; amounts per SI.
rationale: Water is critical for mesopore formation in ZIF systems. Removing or replacing H2O with weaker bases (EtOH, glycol, MeCN, DMF) gave solid/non-mesoporous products; adding NH3·H2O caused irregular ZIF-90 nanoparticles. Similar no-water failures occurred for ZIF-8 and ZIF-67.
solvent_main_amount_text: 2 mL (Zn salt solution) plus H2O fraction within 2 mL H2O/MeOH 6:1 (linker solution)

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Direct mixing of Ln(NO3)3 with H2fum and H2bdc gave precipitated powders; hydrothermal method was needed for crystals.
mof_description: a samarium metal-organic framework with dinuclear {Ln2(OCO)6(H2O)4} units; 2-fold interpenetrated and pcu topology built by organic linkers fumaric acid and terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Direct mixing (no hydrothermal heating) gave precipitated powders. Ambient 20–30 °C and 0.5–24 h estimated. Metals bundled for part of the 140 °C class (Sm, Eu). Other reagents and amounts per base.
rationale: Ambient direct-mixing of Ln(NO3)3 with H2fum/H2bdc gave precipitated powders; hydrothermal heating produced single-crystal lanthanide CPs (1–14). We map these non-heated conditions as negatives near each temperature-dependent successful base.
stirring: stirred 10 min at RT, then static during heating

modification_notes: Reported: ZrCl4 + DCDPS alone under solvothermal conditions yielded no crystalline product. Built vs PCN-133 by omitting BTB (shift DCDPS into linker_1; linker_2=null). rationale: Negative data include: DCDPS + ZrCl4 alone under solvothermal conditions gave noncrystalline solids; PCN-134 screens sometimes gave noncrystalline powders or alternate PCN-224. We map the DCDPS-only case against the PCN-133 base; alternate-PCN-224 cases are excluded.
activation_text: Activated under vacuum at 100 °C after H2O (1 day) and acetone (2 days) exchange

mof_description: a chromium metal-organic framework with Cr3O oxo-bridged trimer SBU and mtn topology built by organic linker benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Against the microwave biphasic base (Success 7), switch the solvent system to pure water (24 g) and remove 2?pentanol; use either HF or NaF (both 5 mmol) as mineralizer, as both were tested and failed in water (Table 1). rationale: Microwave attempts in pure water did not yield MIL-100(Cr). We represent these as water-only microwave conditions (150 °C, 3 h) using the two fluorine donors (HF or NaF) compared to the successful biphasic/DMF microwave syntheses.

modification_notes: text: MnMOF-2D favoured by increased temperature, time and/or pressure; MnMOF-1 forms at 100 °C under MnMOF-1 protocol (Experimental, MnMOF-1 and MnMOF-2D). Hence 100 °C fails for pure MnMOF-2D.
rationale: Key negatives: L3/L3Me gave no crystalline products; MnMOF-1 conditions drifting (120 °C or 72 h) convert to MnMOF-2D; MnMOF-2D not obtained at 100 °C; L2 shows poor solubility and longer times remain non–phase-pure. We map these failures around MnMOF-1/2D, MnMOF-L2, and related systems.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: ZrOCl2 + 100 equiv formic/acetic acid: no crystals; lowering modulator gave amorphous; UiO-66-87 sample was amorphous.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 nodes (UiO-66) built by organic linkers terephthalic acid and adipic acid
modification_notes: From Fig. 2/SI: UiO-66-87 (BDC 0.1 mmol; adipic acid 1.9 mmol) made under the same ZrCl4 + aq. HCl/DMF solvothermal protocol was amorphous (broad PXRD). Represented vs UiO-66-69 by changing linker amounts to those of UiO-66-87.
rationale: Negative conditions captured: ZrOCl2 with 100 equiv formic/acetic acid gave no crystals; decreasing those modulators gave amorphous solids; UiO-66-87 (high adipate load) was amorphous under the HCl/ZrCl4 route; attempts with succinic acid co-linker gave no incorporation.
washing_cycles: Rinse DMF ~5 mL; rinse EtOH ~20 mL; H2O 20 mL at 80 °C for 2 h, then rinse H2O
activation_text: dried at 60 °C in oven for 1 h

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Direct reactions of H3L and DABCO with mixed Zn(II)/Cu(II) salts gave unidentifiable precipitates; mixed-metal MOFs not obtained by direct synthesis.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with Zn2(CO2)4 paddlewheel SBU; DABCO pillars built by organic linkers [1,1?:3?,1?-terphenyl]-4,4?,5?-tricarboxylic acid and 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane
modification_notes: Article states that reactions of H3L and DABCO with mixed Zn(II) and Cu(II) salts under the same Zn-1 solvothermal conditions (DMF/EtOH 1:1, HCl to clarity, 90 °C, 3 d) gave unidentifiable precipitates; bimetallic frameworks could not be obtained by direct synthesis. Represented by adding a Cu(II) salt alongside Zn(NO3)2. The paper did not specify the Cu salt identity or amount; per class-substitution allowance, several common Cu(II) salts are listed as representatives and their amounts are left unset.
rationale: Paper reports Zn-1 via solvothermal DMF/EtOH with HCl. Direct mixed-Zn/Cu solvothermal attempts with H3L and DABCO gave unidentifiable precipitates; bimetallic Zn–Cu frameworks only via metathesis. We capture the failed direct mixed-metal syntheses against the Zn-1 base.
modulator_1_amount_text: added until the mixture turned clear

modification_notes: At 120 °C with Zr:BDC=1:2, removing water from the successful 1:2:3_120-UiO base (success 3) reproduces 1:2:0_120-UiO, which is reported as UiO-66 with poorer crystallinity and ill-defined shapes; degraded target treated as a failure.
rationale: Water controls phase in Zr–BDC solvothermal syntheses. rationale: Targeting ZIF-8 at a 1:4 ligand:metal ratio in water required DMF. Omitting DMF (D0) yielded the nonporous dia(Zn) polymorph instead of ZIF-8. We represent this as a DMF-omission failure relative to the ZIF-8 base recipe.

mof_description: a molybdenum metal-organic framework with Mo–O–Zn bimetallic oxide network; {Zn6Mo6} 12-membered rings built by organic linker 3-amino-1,2,4-triazole
modification_notes: Off-target pH trials: authors report that unless pH ? 4.0, no product or very low yield results. Represented via pH-as-modulator-identity substitution: lower pH by using HCl instead of NaOH; raise pH by using a stronger base (tetramethylammonium hydroxide, TMAH) instead of NaOH. All other conditions held as in the successful hydrothermal recipe.
rationale: For [Zn3(3atrz)2(H2O)2(MoO4)2]n, the paper states pH must be about 4.0; outside this, no product or very low yield. We represent off-pH conditions by substituting the pH-adjusting modulator: acidify (HCl) or over-basic (stronger base, TMAH).

modification_notes: Substitute the successful defective linker (3-FBA, 10 mmol) with 3-aminobenzoic acid (3-ABA, 10 mmol) under the same solvothermal conditions (DMF/EtOH/H2O = 1:1:1; 100 °C; 12 h). The paper reports Cu-BTC-ABA shows a completely different PXRD and a disrupted Cu-BTC structure with green crystals (failure).
rationale: Negative condition: introducing 3-aminobenzoic acid (3-ABA) as the defective linker disrupted the Cu-BTC framework (Cu-BTC-ABA), unlike the successful Cu-BTC-FBA/HBA/IPA syntheses under identical solvothermal conditions.
stirring: stirred 15 min, then static during heating

article_trial_or_failure_notes: 3-ABA linker destroyed Cu-BTC structure; XRD different and product excluded from study.

stirring: stirred 15 min, then static during heating

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Without nitrate no 1Eu; Na2SO4 gave other solid; H2O2 gave no solid; NaOCl at RT yielded different Eu3+ solid.
mof_description: a europium metal-organic framework built by organic linker fumaric acid
modification_notes: Remove nitrate from the EuCl3-based hydrothermal recipe (160 °C, 12 h). The article states that EuCl3 + fumaric acid at pH 1–2 without nitrate did not yield 1Eu under the same hydrothermal conditions.
rationale: Negative conditions for forming [Eu2(fum)2(ox)(H2O)4]·4H2O were extracted: removing nitrate with EuCl3, replacing nitrate by H2O2 or Na2SO4 under identical hydrothermal conditions, and using NaOCl at room temperature for 3 days. A no-Ln3+ control is recorded but unrepresentable in the schema.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Without nitrate no 1Eu; Na2SO4 gave other solid; H2O2 gave no solid; NaOCl at RT yielded different Eu3+ solid.
mof_description: a terbium metal-organic framework built by organic linker fumaric acid
modification_notes: General requirement: “hydrothermal conditions are needed to form oxalate in situ” and nitrate/hypochlorite is indispensable (Conclusion). Thus, RT fails; absence of nitrate (TbCl3 instead of nitrate) is expected to fail under the same protocol.
rationale: For [Ln2(fum)2(ox)(H2O)4]·4H2O (Ln=Eu, Gd, Tb), failures arise without nitrate, with unsuitable oxidants (H2O2, Na2SO4), and under non-hydrothermal conditions (NaOCl at room temperature). These negatives document oxalate formation requirements and temperature dependence for 1Eu/1Gd/1Tb formation.

mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework with Fe(III)-oxo clusters with ?3-O built by organic linker benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Parallel synthesis without glycol under the otherwise identical 80 °C, 2 h DMF/glycol protocol (Fig. S3) did not yield MIL-100(Fe) nanospheres; the product was not identified. Authors conclude glycol is indispensable. Represented by removing glycol from the mixed solvent.
rationale: MIL-100(Fe) nanospheres form in DMF/glycol at 80 °C, 2 h. A parallel experiment without glycol did not yield MIL-100(Fe) nanospheres, indicating glycol is indispensable. We represent the no-glycol condition as a negative case against the successful base.

modification_notes: Direct solvothermal attempts to replace Zn2+ with Cu2+ or Ni2+ under the base conditions (DMF 15 mL, 120 °C, 48 h) were reported as not successful. rationale: Negative conditions cover direct solvothermal attempts to prepare Cu- and Ni-analogues of the Zn-MOF under the same DMF/120 °C/48 h recipe; these were reported as not successful. Post-synthetic ion-exchange trials are excluded.

modification_notes: Built against the JUC-58 base. Substituted Mn(II) with Co(II) or Ni(II) at the same amount and omitted glycol (DMF only). modification_notes: Against the successful 4-Brip + bpe hydrothermal recipe (H2O, KOH, 130 °C, 3 d), replace bpe with bpp (same molar amount as base). The article states this pairing gave only unknown precipitates. Amount for bpp carried over as 0.1 mmol per one-for-one substitution convention.
rationale: One failed attempt is reported: 4-bromoisophthalate with bpp and Mn(II) gave only unknown precipitates. Represented as a substitution against the successful 4-Brip + bpe hydrothermal recipe.

modification_notes: Failures tied to solvent choice: text: “using less polar ethanol as a solvent, there was no significant morphological change … the milky white slurry of ZIF-8 did not become clear or transparent after continuous CO2 gas bubbling” (Fig. 4a–c). Text: “using water as a solvent, CO2 gas bubbling led to the formation of … Znx(mim)x(CO3)x, rather than ZIF-8” (Fig. 4a,e; Table S4).

time_text: CO2 bubbling 30 min (70 mL/min), then stirred 30 min after stopping CO2

Shear-related failures exist but are outside allowed classes.
stirring: shear homogenized at 11,500 rpm for 2 min; then static at 4 °C
crystal_size: ~1 μm scale (similar to ZIF-8 with SPAN-80)

mof_description: a nickel metal-organic framework with octahedral Ni nodes; 2D layers linked by bpy and btc built by organic linkers 4,4'-bipyridine and 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylate
modification_notes: Direct failures: text states “reactions, with benzene, toluene, cyclohexane, pyrene, or anthracene, all produced guest-free 2 or 4 as the only crystalline product.” Also, “compound 2 is the only product when naphthalene is absent.” We vary hydrophobic guests under the same hydrothermal protocol.
rationale: In the Ni(II)–bpy–btc hydrothermal system, guest-incorporated frameworks (1, 3) require naphthalene. Substituting benzene, toluene, cyclohexane, pyrene, or anthracene yielded only guest-free 2 or 4. Without naphthalene, only 2 forms irrespective of composition. We compile these explicit non-working guest conditions.
metal_cluster_connectivity: octahedral Ni nodes; 2D layers linked by bpy and btc

modification_notes: Direct failures: text states “reactions, with benzene, toluene, cyclohexane, pyrene, or anthracene, all produced guest-free 2 or 4 as the only crystalline product.” Also, “compound 2 is the only product when naphthalene is absent.” We vary hydrophobic guests under the same hydrothermal protocol.
rationale: In the Ni(II)–bpy–btc hydrothermal system, guest-incorporated frameworks (1, 3) require naphthalene. Substituting benzene, toluene, cyclohexane, pyrene, or anthracene yielded only guest-free 2 or 4. Without naphthalene, only 2 forms irrespective of composition. We compile these explicit non-working guest conditions.
metal_cluster_connectivity: octahedral Ni nodes; 2D layers linked by bpy and btc

article_trial_or_failure_notes: RT 1:1 Ni/Co and RT 2:1 Ni gave 1D chain, not CPO-27; only RT 2:1 Co formed CPO-27-Co.
mof_description: a nickel metal-organic framework with 1D M–O octahedra rod SBU with open metal sites built by organic linker 2,5-dihydroxyterephthalic acid
modification_notes: Bounded failure: PXRD shows no crystalline CPO-27 below 110 °C (Fig. 4). Main text and SI show 2:1 Ni at room temperature gives the 1D chain, not CPO-27 (text; SI §5.2, 7.2).
rationale: For CPO-27-Ni and -Co, PXRD shows no crystalline CPO-27 below 110 °C, and room-temperature equimolar mixtures give a 1D chain [(M(H2dhtp)(H2O)4)·2H2O]; only Co 2:1 at RT yields CPO-27-Co. We therefore enumerate sub-110 °C and RT equimolar conditions as negative outcomes.
time_text: 30 min to 24 h; product typically after ~2 h
vessel_type: Teflon insert sealed in steel autoclave
stirring: stirred 5 min before sealing; then static
metal_cluster_connectivity: 1D M–O octahedra rod SBU with open metal sites

modification_notes: text: “When the amount of p-TA goes on increasing, it is not available to obtain any sample.” SI Table S1 lists to p-TA-20; main text: p-TA-20 extremely low yield; higher gave no sample.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: High-throughput screening at 180 °C showed domains where MIL-118A, MIL-120, or mixtures formed instead of MIL-121.
mof_description: an aluminum metal-organic framework with trans-connected AlO4(OH)2 octahedral chains (rod SBU) built by organic linker pyromellitic acid
modification_notes: Evidence: Fig. 3 and text: “MIL-121 appears in concentrated Al solutions whereas MIL-118A crystallized in a narrower domain in diluted Al solutions… MIL-120 formed at higher pH (NaOH).” Also: “In presence of NaOH… existence domain of MIL-121 is much smaller; decreasing Al concentration led to mixtures; MIL-120 obtained as pure form for diluted Al systems.”
rationale: HT mapping of Al–H4btec–H2O(–NaOH) showed MIL-121 only in concentrated Al, while diluted Al or added NaOH gave MIL-118A, MIL-120, or mixtures. We list pH-raising NaOH and dilution/composition shifts that disfavor MIL-121 formation.
activation_text: heated at 380 °C for 5 h; degassed at 200 °C under 5 Pa vacuum for 15 h prior to N2 sorption

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Further attempts to get suitable single crystals by different methods failed.
mof_description: a lead metal-organic framework with hemidirected PbII nodes (five- and six-coordinate) built by organic linker (S)-5-(((1-carboxy-3-methylbutyl)amino)methyl)isophthalic acid
modification_notes: Text: “Further attempts to get suitable single crystals by different methods failed.” Around the 110 °C, 72 h protocol with post-evaporation, changing solvothermal temperature and time failed to give suitable single crystals.
rationale: Across Pb–H3L1 (1), Pb–H3L2 (2), Cd–H3L2 (3), and Pb–H3L3 (4), the authors note “Further attempts to get suitable single crystals by different methods failed.” We therefore enumerate off-window temperatures and times that were tried to improve crystallinity but did not yield suitable single crystals.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Only 1/10 syntheses gave phase-pure PCN-222; no ordered PCN-224 obtained (3/10 were phase-pure dPCN-224); many mixtures or amorphous.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 8-connected SBU and csq topology built by organic linker tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin
modification_notes: Basis: PCN-222 recipe (DEF/benzoic acid, 120 °C, 48 h). Evidence: text and Fig. 2/S5–S7 show many non-PCN-222 outcomes under identical conditions; text: “increased reaction times at 145 °C favored PCN-222 … whereas the converse result was obtained at 120 °C” (Refs. 27, 28) implying longer times at 120 °C disfavor PCN-222.
rationale: Round-robin syntheses of Zr–porphyrin MOFs showed poor phase selectivity: only 1/10 phase-pure PCN-222; ordered PCN-224 never obtained (only dPCN-224). Literature within text indicates strong time–temperature sensitivity near 120–145 °C; we prioritize longer-time failures for PCN-222 at 120 °C.
activation_text: 8 M HCl (0.2 mL) in DMF (3 mL), 100 °C for 24 h; then 3×4 mL DMF wash, overnight DMF soak, 4×5 mL acetone; dry in air

modification_notes: Text: “The use of 4-pyridinecarboxylic acid in this reaction leads only to compound 1. Therefore, it is necessary to employ 4-cyanopyridine to obtain single crystals of compound 3.” Treat 4-Hpyc as a failed linker under same solvothermal protocol.
rationale: Paper reports that 2b fails under THF reflux and that 3 requires ≥8 h under microwave; shorter times give mixtures. For solvothermal 3, substituting 4-cyanopyridine with 4-pyridinecarboxylic acid yields 1 instead, not 3. Negative points are drawn from Table 1 and text.
activation_text: Outgassed at 303 K under vacuum for 60 h (for adsorption)

article_trial_or_failure_notes: m4-ZIF-4 (1-MeIm:Im = 1:0) gave 0% yield; no product with 1-MeIm as sole linker.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework built by organic linker imidazole
modification_notes: Explicit failure: m4-ZIF-4 (1-MeIm:Im = 1:0) produced no product. Evidence: text: “no formation of product when using 1-MeIm as the sole linker”; SI Table S5: m4-ZIF-4 yield 0%. Same solvent, temperature, and time as success.
rationale: Paper probes ZIF-4 and m1-, m2-, m3-ZIF-4 using 1-methylimidazole as modulator. Explicit failure: m4-ZIF-4 (1-MeIm:Im = 1:0) gives no product. We compile negative conditions centered on the sole-1-MeIm case for these syntheses.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: One-pot hydrothermal reaction of CoCl2, Ce(NO3)3, and H2Pzdc failed to obtain 2.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework with CoII 4-connected node; CeIII 3-connected; 3D herringbone net built by organic linker pyrazine 2,3-dicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Explicit failure captured: main text states “an attempt of one-pot reaction of CoCl2, Ce(NO3)3, and H2Pzdc fail to obtain compound 2.” Interpreted as replacing metalloligand 1 with free H2Pzdc and adding Co2+ salt under the same hydrothermal conditions (pH≈7, H2O).
rationale: Targeting {[Ce2Co(Pzdc)4(H2O)6]·2H2O}n (2). The paper explicitly states that a one-pot hydrothermal reaction of CoCl2, Ce(NO3)3, and H2Pzdc failed, while stepwise synthesis via metalloligand 1 worked. We encode that explicit failed condition against the successful protocol.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Using EtOH with Cu(NO3)2·3H2O as metal source gave non–phase-pure products (extra PXRD peaks; Fig. S6).
mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework built by organic linkers benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid and isophthalic acid
modification_notes: Nitrate-series note: “When EtOH was used, phase purity was not obtained (see Figure S6).” Although S6 illustrates D7/D8, this statement is made under the Cu(NO3)2·3H2O section (D5–D8), implying EtOH fails with nitrate precursor.
rationale: The paper shows that EtOH with Cu(NO3)2·3H2O gives non–phase-pure [Cu3(BTC)2–x(IP)x] (extra PXRD peaks; SI Fig. S6/S20). DMF works for nitrate-based DEMOFs and both DMF/EtOH work for Cu(BF4)2-based DEMOFs. No other clear failing windows are reported for HKUST-1 or BF4-based DEMOFs.
activation_text: 140 °C under dynamic vacuum (~1e-3 mbar) for 24 h

rationale: ZIF-94 at room temperature requires long reaction time for phase purity: “Only after 16 h is a phase pure material produced; times <16 h show ZIF-93.” Negative conditions focus on sub-16 h times under the reported THF/MeOH protocol.

modification_notes: Evidence: SI S1.2 Table S1 (“metal salt, M:L ratio, concentration, reaction time” screened to optimize InOF-2). article_trial_or_failure_notes: Attempts to convert 1a to 1b in the aqueous medium at 50–60 °C were not successful.
mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework with bis-aminoalcoholate dicopper [Cu2(µ-Hmdea)2]2+ subunits; 2-connected Cu and dia topology built by organic linkers N-methyldiethanolamine and pyromellitic acid
modification_notes: Direct text evidence: (i) At ~25 °C the reaction gives 1a as sole product (main text, Synthesis of 1a and 1b); (ii) attempts to convert 1a to 1b in aqueous medium at 50–60 °C were not successful (main text). Also, replacing KOH with excess H2mdea (0.573 mL, 5 mmol) produces 1a (main text).
rationale: For [{Cu2(µ-Hmdea)2}2(µ4-pma)]n (1b), ~60 °C in water is required. At ~25 °C the same system affords 1a exclusively, and attempts to convert 1a to 1b at 50–60 °C in aqueous medium failed. Using excess H2mdea (5 mmol) instead of KOH yields 1a.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Increasing Fe content failed; Fe BDC formed instead of Fe Cr-MIL-101.
mof_description: an iron metal-organic framework built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Based on Cr-MIL-101 hydrothermal/HF recipe. Text evidence: “Attempts to increase amounts of Fe … not succeeded. Thus … Fe-BDC was formed.” We introduce Fe beyond 25 wt% (of total metal) under identical conditions; reported to yield Fe-BDC, not Fe–Cr-MIL-101.

modification_notes: Swap the rigid linear linker 7a to the thiophene-carboxylated isomer 7b. Evidence: text, “Initial attempts to synthesize a framework using 7b have been unsuccessful…”. Conditions mirrored from the successful Zn(NO3)2·6H2O/DMF solvothermal protocol.
rationale: UBMOF-1 forms from Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and linker 7a (TPDC) in DMF at 110 °C, 48 h. The paper states attempts with linker 7b failed to give a framework. We enumerate that explicit failure under the successful solvothermal protocol to capture negative conditions for UBMOF-1 attempts.

mof_description: a terbium metal-organic framework with Ln2(–COO)4 4-connected dimer and dia topology built by organic linker biphenyl-4,4'-dicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Evidence: Experimental 2.2.1 states H3L is insoluble in water, methanol, ethanol, acetone, acetonitrile, dichloromethane, chloroform; only DMF/DMSO dissolve it, implying failed crystallization in those solvents. rationale: For (Me2NH2)2(H3O)[LnL2] (Ln = Eu, Gd, Tb), failures are implied when H3L is used in solvents where it is insoluble. The text also reports amorphous powder when replacing 2,2′-DSBPDC with H3L under the prior DSBPDC protocol.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Hydrothermal screen 100–200 °C performed; raising pH >7 with ethylenediamine/NaOH gave powdery/black solids and no single crystals.
mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework built by organic linkers 1,4-naphthalenediphosphonic acid and 4,4'-bipyridine
modification_notes: Direct SI failure: “Increasing the pH using ethylenediamine and NaOH above 7 resulted in powdery phases and black sticky solids and no single crystals.” Applied to the successful aqueous recipe for compound 1 at 120 °C, 2 days.
rationale: Hydrothermal syntheses of Cu–naphthalene diphosphonate frameworks 1–3 were pH-sensitive. SI states raising pH above 7 using ethylenediamine or NaOH yielded powdery/black solids and no single crystals. Negative conditions therefore center on basic modulators under the same aqueous protocols.
vessel_type: Teflon-lined Parr acid digestion vessel (23 mL)

mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with Zr6O4(OH)4 12-connected SBU built by organic linker CuTCPP
modification_notes: SAS low-modulator boundary (100–200 eq.) reported as unsuccessful (text; SI S13–S15). Added here as negative options.
rationale: Explicit failures: SAS Fe-MOF-525 at low methacrylic acid loadings (100–200 eq.) gave amorphous polymer, no crystalline MOF. article_trial_or_failure_notes: At concentrations above 1.1 M (TFA) and 1.2 M (DCA), no product observed after 18 h at 90 °C.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework with fcu topology built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Main text: “At concentrations above 1.1 and 1.2 M for TFA and DCA, respectively, no product was observed after 18 h at 90 °C.” Also ranges used: TFA 0.62–1.2 M; DCA 0.3–1.1 M. Swap AA to over-limit TFA/DCA → no product.
rationale: For UiO-66, Morris et al. report that using DCA or TFA above specific concentration thresholds yields no product after 18 h at 90 °C in DMF. We enumerate those non-working modulator loadings against the successful UiO-66 solvothermal protocol.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Phase screening showed coexisting phases at certain H2O volumes and temperatures; pure phases only outside those ranges.
mof_description: a manganese metal-organic framework with mononuclear Mn2+ octahedra built by organic linker 4,4'-stilbenedicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: Evidence: text and Fig. 5, Fig. S7a: H2O/DMF > 1:9 needed for Mn-sdc-2 at 160 °C; below this or in coexisting ranges yields Mn-sdc-1 or mixed phases. Synthesis section shows DMF 10 mL + acetic acid gives Mn-sdc-1 (not Mn-sdc-2).
rationale: Negative conditions stem from the H2O/DMF-dependent phase diagram: Mn-sdc-1 and Mn-sdc-2 interconvert with coexisting-phase windows. We enumerate solvent and temperature settings that give Mn-sdc-2 or mixed phases instead of the targeted Mn-sdc-1 or Mn-sdc-2.

mof_description: a copper metal-organic framework with Cu2+ trigonal-bipyramidal, mononuclear 4-connected node; HL2− 4-connected linker built by organic linker triphosphaazatriangulene
modification_notes: Basis: text ‘exposed to water vapor… completely converted into 1’’ within 12 h’ (main text; SI S7–S8). SI Fig. S4: 120–140 °C in vacuo alters PXRD; recovery requires DMSO/MeOH. Hence H2O-rich or no DMSO and high T conditions do not afford MOF 1 under bulk synthesis.
rationale: For [Cu(HL)(DMSO)·(MeOH)]n (1), water disrupts DMSO coordination and converts 1 to 1''. SI shows high-temperature treatment (120–140 °C, in vacuo) alters PXRD. Thus H2O-rich or DMSO-free media and overly high temperatures are negative for forming 1.
activation_text: room temperature under vacuum for 3 h (to give [Cu(HL)(DMSO)]n); for measurements sometimes further activated at RT under 1.0×10^-4 Pa for 12 h
metal_cluster_connectivity: Cu2+ trigonal-bipyramidal, mononuclear 4-connected node; HL2− 4-connected linker

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Fresh DMF gave a mixture including MOF-5 analogue; excess [NH2R2]Cl led to product contaminated with unreacted H2bdc.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with Zn3(μ-O2CR)6 SBU; 3D network built by organic linker terephthalic acid
modification_notes: General experimental: “Addition of larger amounts of [NH2Et2]Cl ... led to product contaminated with unreacted H2bdc.” Also, text: without additive in fresh DEF, 1 forms instead of 2.
rationale: For Zn–bdc systems, solvent hydrolysis and dialkylammonium templates switch products: MOF-5 (1) vs [NH2Et2]2[Zn3(bdc)4]·2.5DEF (2) vs [NH2Me2]2[Zn3(bdc)4]·DMF·H2O (3). Fresh DMF gave mixtures; excess [NH2R2]Cl caused contamination with unreacted H2bdc. We enumerate these negative conditions per successful base.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: 1·H2O only obtained via three-step SCSC; one- or two-step attempts failed
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with Zn2 paddle-wheel 4-connected nodes; linker 8-connected and scu topology built by organic linker 5,5′-(2,2-bis((3,5-dicarboxyphenoxy)methyl)propane-1,3-diyl)bis(oxy)diisophthalic acid
modification_notes: Evidence: same-conditions solvent screen maps DMF→1·DMF; DMA, DEA, DMP, DEP give 2–5 instead; DMSO/EtOH gives 1·DMSO (text; Fig. 2). Thus these solvents fail to afford 1·DMF under the one-pot protocol.
rationale: Solvent dictates phase: DMSO/EtOH gives 1·DMSO; DMF gives 1·DMF; DMA→2; DEA→3; DMP→4; DEP→5. Thus, swapping to other named solvents under identical one‑pot conditions fails to yield the target phase. Also, 1·H2O required three-step SCSC; one- or two-step routes failed.
activation_text: Dichloromethane exchange 24 h; dried under dynamic vacuum at room temperature overnight; outgas 12 h at room temperature

modification_notes: Evidence: SI Fig. S8 shows acetic acid gives the Zr-cca phase; benzoic acid (main text, Experimental; SI Figs. S5, S8) also gives Zr-cca. Both modulators fail to form Zr-cca-FA. rationale: Modulator identity controls phase in this Zr/H2cca system: benzoic or acetic acid give Zr-cca, while formic acid yields a different phase (Zr-cca-FA) and resisted SCXRD crystal growth despite optimization. modification_notes: Text: “Similarly, addition of bpe to Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and H2L2 under solvothermal conditions consistently gives phase-pure 2…” Heating the RT recipe (5) to solvothermal conditions fails to give 5 (yields 2).
rationale: Solvothermal addition of bpe or bpy with H2L1, and bpe with H2L2, failed to incorporate N-heterocycles, yielding MOFs 1 or 2. Conversely, heating conditions prevent formation of room-temperature bpe frameworks 4 and 5. No explicit negative variants were reported for 3.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Competing phase [Zn2(hett)+] formed when H2O <3% during MUF-77-ethyl synthesis; eliminated by adding MUF-77-ethyl seed crystals.
mof_description: a zinc metal-organic framework with Zn4O 6-connected SBU built by organic linkers 5,5′,10,10′,15,15′-hexaethyltruxene-2,7,12-tricarboxylic acid, biphenyl-4,4'-dicarboxylic acid and terephthalic acid
modification_notes: Direct failure: SI S14(b) states “when water content is lower than 3% … a rod shaped MOF [Zn2(hett)+] … competing phase” (eliminated by seeding). We list concrete sub-3% H2O volumes in 1.0 mL DEF that yield the competing phase.
rationale: From Liu & Telfer (2015), only MUF-77-ethyl shows an explicit synthesis failure: H2O <3% v/v in DEF gives competing [Zn2(hett)+]. Other MUF-77 variants and MUF-7a lack reported failed solvothermal parameters. We therefore enumerate the substantiated low-water failures for MUF-77-ethyl.
activation_text: Solvent exchange with CH2Cl2, then 80 °C under vacuum for 10 h

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Formic acid or K2CO3 decomposed the Ir complex; ZrOCl2 gave poorer crystallinity; 80–90 °C gave only amorphous solids.
mof_description: a zirconium metal-organic framework built by organic linkers 2,2’-bipyridine-5,5’-dicarboxylic acid and biphenyl-4,4'-dicarboxylic acid
modification_notes: One-pot Method D base. Failures to include: formic acid or K2CO3 decomposed Ir complex (text); replacing ZrCl4 with ZrOCl2 led to poorer crystallinity (SI Fig. S6.2.2). Lower T (80–90 °C) produced amorphous solids under similar DMF/H2O conditions (SI).
rationale: For UiO-67 functionalised with Ir (and Ir+Pd/Rh), failures include: additives (formic acid, K2CO3) decomposed the Ir complex; ZrOCl2 gave poorer crystallinity; and 80–90 °C produced only amorphous solids. Negative conditions target these factors around the successful DMF/H2O solvothermal protocols.

article_trial_or_failure_notes: Adding Ln(NO3)3·nH2O aimed for Co–Ln CPs but only Co CP 1 formed; Ln not incorporated.
mof_description: a cobalt metal-organic framework with linear trinuclear Co3(COO)6 6-connected SBU built by organic linker 3,5-bis(4-carboxyphenyl)pyridine
modification_notes: Vary solvent system only. Evidence: text: “the introduction and decomposition of DMF plays an important role in the formation of 1”; “different reaction solvents lead to the distinct structures of Co(bcpp) (hydrothermal H2O) and [Co3(bcpp)3(OH)]·guest (DMA) and 1.” Hence H2O-only and DMA-only are implied non-working for 1. Text: “introduction of Ln(NO3)3·nH2O has no obvious effect on the formation of 1.”
rationale: Formation of Co3(bcpp)2(HCOO)2(H2O)2 depends on DMF decomposition to formate; solvent choice is decisive. Using DMA or water-only leads to different Co–bcpp phases or no Co3 cluster. Adding Ln(NO3)3·nH2O had no effect on making 1, confirming solvent-direction is key.

modification_notes: Anion swap failures: text: 'Addition of F−, Br−, I−, PO4 3− (NH4F, NH4Br, NH4I or Na3PO4 were used instead of t-BuNH3Cl at the same reaction conditions) ...
